mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 5% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If unemployment exceeds 5% but S&P 500 returns remain positive.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rises while employment stays flat, it indicates labor market stress, leading to negative returns.
failure_condition: If labor market stress signals occur but returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, higher FEDFUNDS rates negatively impact equity valuations, leading to lower returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rise but S&P 500 returns increase.

mechanism_narrative: Higher inflation leads to increased costs and reduced consumer spending, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If inflation rises but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production signals reduced economic output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If industrial production falls but returns remain positive.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts increasing without corresponding retail sales growth indicates economic imbalance, leading to negative returns.
failure_condition: If housing starts rise without retail sales growth but returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing GDP growth in late-cycle expansion signals impending economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If GDP growth slows but S&P 500 returns remain positive.
